model_interpretation.claim: A portable eight-byte bit-plane validator can check starter classes, required continuation positions, and restricted second-byte ranges across the whole stream, carrying only the few requirements that cross block boundaries. This contrasts with the selected parent, which skips ASCII blocks but scalar-decodes mixed blocks; it may reduce mixed-block scalar control flow, though the mask setup could cost more. Keep the strict scalar validator for the tail and any final sequence crossing the buffer boundary.

model_interpretation.claim: The catalog has three distinct, valid SIMD-scan programs and no repeats, but none beat the 49.62 µs baseline: the 16-byte scan measured 60.43 µs, the selected lane-bisection parent 77.82 µs, and the 64-byte variant 81.00 µs. This contrasting SIMD-prefix/scalar-remainder hybrid tests whether repeatedly restarting SIMD scans and locating a lane after each decoded code point costs more than it saves. It skips only complete 16-byte ASCII vectors; on the first vector containing any high bit, it sends the suffix from that block boundary to the strict scalar decoder. This avoids assuming the high-bit byte is a lead and preserves bounded loads, but gives up SIMD scanning of later ASCII runs. Measure it on the official mixed-width n=65536 workload; do not infer a speedup from synthetic inputs.

model_interpretation.claim: A portable 64-bit high-bit mask can skip complete ASCII blocks throughout the buffer. For mixed blocks, scalar-decode through the block boundary and any crossing code point, avoiding both repeated per-byte ASCII checks and the prior full bit-plane classifier's boundary bookkeeping. This hybrid may help when complete ASCII blocks occur often; dense mixed-width data may instead pay the mask-check overhead.

model_interpretation.claim: A portable 8-byte SWAR bit-plane classifier may reduce per-byte control flow on mixed-width inputs by classifying lead and continuation lanes together, comparing shifted continuation requirements, and checking restricted second-byte ranges. If a sequence crosses a block boundary, defer that block and suffix to the strict scalar validator instead of carrying state. This contrasts with the selected T1 parent's ASCII-block skip and the earlier carry-state variants; it is an unmeasured experiment, not a claimed speedup.

items.subject: Whole-stream SIMD UTF-8 validation with cross-block state
items.objective: Primary hypothesis: SIMD masks validate UTF-8 constraints across the whole buffer, unlike T2's ASCII-span locator. Explore block classification, shifted continuation requirements, restricted second-byte checks, cross-block state, and a bounded tail. Compare relevant SIMD variants only when supported by the frozen target and unchanged build; do not alter flags or add runtime environment probing. Keep the supplied scalar implementation as a control, and report any useful hybrid as a distinct variant rather than excluding it. Preserve exact scalar-value validation, ABI, output, and thread budget. Use the official mixed-width n=65536 timing for performance and official ASCII/malformed checks for correctness, paying particular attention to vector boundaries and truncations where covered. Record failed variants.
